headline: Interview with Jack Black About Kung Fu Panda By Publimetro
content: Youve been voicing Po for over six years now… Its actually more like ten. Before animation began, I started recording his voice. During these years, my involvement with pandas increased due to working on the project, though not obsessively. How does martial arts appeal to you? Martial arts fascinate me—I love the genre and films within it. While I wouldnt call myself a master, I defend well enough while mimicking some moves. Do you see yourself as a good teacher? Yes, teaching requires temperament and patience which I believe I possess. Teaching involves learning too—a lesson still being learned through making ‘Kung Fu Panda 3’. This panda grows up becoming a master, reflecting lessons were also learning. When you record Po’s voice, how physically involved do you get? When told Po practices kung-fu during certain scenes, moving accordingly makes him sound far more realistic—even running helps capture authenticity. Is crafting characters using just physical language harder than doing so solely vocally? Acting out loud demands early mornings filled with dressing and makeup—its stressful compared to relaxed voice sessions where mastery feels achievable. Where did inspiration come from initially creating Pos unique voice? Nobody asked specifically—they wanted something different from another animated character voiced previously. They requested a familiar tone akin to what was heard in ‘School of Rocks’. Does Po resonate personally since he embodies unexpected bravery? Indeed, Po represents innocence-driven courage—the kind seen in children unaware of danger yet daringly climbing trees despite potential harm. His innocent perspective brings both strength and folly. Pandas were part of your journey beyond movies—is there ongoing interest post-project? My attention towards pandas grew thanks to this experience, although obsession isn’t quite accurate. Humor plays differently across cultures—how important is it universally? Humorous elements often struggle crossing linguistic barriers, losing meaning along translations. However, themes explored in ‘Kung Fu Panda’, such as adventure and emotional depth between father and child, translate better globally. These aspects make comedy less reliant purely upon jokes alone.

headline: Here And Now, New Album By Peruvian Singer Nina Mutual Presented Tonight In Barranco

headline: Remembering Sir George Martin, Producer Behind Most Beatle Albums Except One
content: British music producer George Martin passed away at age ninety after contributing significantly to nearly every Beatles track except ‘Let It Be.’ Former band member Ringo Starr announced his passing with deep sadness. Paul McCartney expressed gratitude toward Martin who guided the group skillfully throughout their career. Many regard Martin fittingly as the fifth Beatle given his extensive influence behind iconic hits reaching number ones worldwide.
